title: Finite-free stupid tails are perfect
statement: Let X be any scheme [def-pc-scheme] and K a bounded-above cochain complex of finite free structure-sheaf modules. For every integer r, replace its terms below r by zero and keep the remaining terms and differentials. The derived image of this explicit stupid tail is perfect [def-pc-derived-category, def-pc-perfect-complex].

source.place: Tag 08EG, proof of Lemma 36.13.6, finite-free lift and stupid truncation; read online at https://stacks.math.columbia.edu/tag/08EG

proof.text: The termwise stupid-truncation isomorphisms identify each term in degree at least r with the corresponding term of K; terms below r are zero. Thus the tail is zero outside [r,b], where b is the supplied upper bound.

Restrict to the top open. The over-site restriction preserves zero objects, finite coproducts, and the unit sheaf. Mathlib SheafOfModules.mapFreeIso transports each supplied finite-free isomorphism, giving a finite-free retract in every retained degree, and a zero-rank retract in each vanished degree. This gives IsStrictlyPerfect directly by [def-pc-perfect-complex]. The mapDerivedCategoryFactors comparison supplies the required local model for every point, proving IsPerfect. The Lean proof is complete.

theorem finiteFree_stupidTail_isPerfect
    (X : Scheme.{u})
    [HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ V : X.Opens,
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} ((moduleRings X.toRingedSpace).over V))]
    (K : CochainComplex (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings X.toRingedSpace)) ℤ)
    (hbounded : ∃ N : ℤ, ∀ i : ℤ, N < i → IsZero (K.X i))
    (hfree : ∀ i : ℤ, ∃ m : ℕ, Nonempty (K.X i ≅ SheafOfModules.free
      (R := moduleRings X.toRingedSpace) (ULift.{u} (Fin m))))
    (r : ℤ) :
    IsPerfect X (DerivedCategory.Q.obj (K.stupidTrunc (ComplexShape.embeddingUpIntGE r)))
